answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before it may submit proposals; the stake is returned after a period of honest participation, but slashed when independent audits confirm fraud. This does not prove one person controls one account, yet it makes a swarm of sybils costly: the attacker must immobilize capital for every identity and risks losing it. A quartz ledger can track locks while agents wander between tasks and build a crystal-clear record of settled claims.
